_comment: Member directories to harvest. Each network's tags are fixed here, never inferred per member: LTA members all hold land, Waterkeeper licensees all have enforcement capacity. 'url' must be a machine-readable directory endpoint confirmed from Actions - the placeholders below are marked needs_endpoint and are skipped until filled.

networks.label: Land Trust Alliance member land trusts
networks.desc: WHAT IT DOES: {name}, a land trust serving {where} and a member of the Land Trust Alliance - it buys land outright and holds conservation easements that permanently retire development rights while land stays in private hands. USE IT honestly: land trusts are NOT campaigning organisations and will not oppose a project for you, but they can take the land next to it permanently off the development market, and they know local landowners.

networks.label: Waterkeeper Alliance licensed groups
networks.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: {name}, a licensed Waterkeeper group with a named waterbody to defend. Waterkeepers patrol their water, document pollution, and bring CITIZEN-SUIT enforcement against permit violators - the licence requires enforcement capacity, which is why this network is a route to litigation rather than only advocacy. USE IT: bring them dated, located evidence of a discharge or a permit application.

networks.label: Surfrider Foundation chapters
networks.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: {name}, a Surfrider chapter covering {where}. Chapters organise against coastal development, seawalls, offshore drilling and beach access loss, and routinely appear at coastal commission and local planning hearings. USE IT: strongest where the fight is a coastal permit.

networks.label: ELAW partner public-interest environmental lawyers
networks.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: {name}, a partner in the Environmental Law Alliance Worldwide - a network of PUBLIC-INTEREST environmental lawyers in over 70 countries who represent communities, not project proponents. Partners share scientific and legal expertise across borders, so a group facing a mine or dam can get technical analysis its own country may not supply. USE IT: ask ELAW to connect you to the partner in your country, and to the scientists who have reviewed the same kind of impact assessment elsewhere.

networks.label: Friends of the Earth International national member groups
networks.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: {name}, the Friends of the Earth International member group in {where}. FoEI federates grassroots groups campaigning AGAINST extractive and infrastructure projects and for community land rights, with local groups in most member countries. USE IT: national members can escalate a local fight into an international campaign against the financier or parent company.

networks.label: International Land Coalition members
networks.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: {name}, a member of the International Land Coalition in {where} - a global alliance of civil society and intergovernmental organisations working on people-centred land governance, land rights and defence against land grabbing. USE IT: strongest where the threat is dispossession or an acquisition without consent, and where documented tenure evidence is the lever.

networks.label: La Via Campesina member organisations
networks.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: {name}, a member of La Via Campesina in {where} - an international movement of peasants, small farmers, landless people, Indigenous people and agricultural workers, present in over 80 countries. Members organise directly against land grabbing, evictions and agribusiness expansion. USE IT: where the people losing land are the people who farm it, this network supplies organising capacity rather than legal or grant support.

networks.label: GAIA member grassroots groups (incinerators, landfills, waste)
networks.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: {name}, a member of the Global Alliance for Incinerator Alternatives in {where} — an alliance of 1,000+ GRASSROOTS groups in 90+ countries resisting incinerators, landfills and waste-to-energy plants. Members are overwhelmingly neighbourhood-scale, working the municipal siting and permitting decisions where these facilities are actually approved. USE IT: GAIA members have run their own AIR-QUALITY MONITORING where regulators failed to, which is the evidence a community usually cannot otherwise get.

networks.label: ICCA Consortium members (Indigenous & community conserved territories)
networks.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: {name}, an ICCA Consortium member in {where}. The Consortium supports Indigenous peoples and local communities defending territories they govern and conserve themselves — the unit of organisation is the community territory, not the nation. USE IT where the claim to stop a project rests on customary tenure, self-governance and the right to give or withhold consent.

networks.label: Yes to Life No to Mining solidarity network
networks.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: {name}, part of the Yes to Life No to Mining network in {where} — a global solidarity network of COMMUNITIES REFUSING MINING on their land, rather than negotiating terms. USE IT for the specific question other networks avoid: how communities say no outright, and what has worked when they did.

networks.label: Global Forest Coalition member organisations
networks.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: {name}, a Global Forest Coalition member in {where} — a coalition of NGOs and Indigenous peoples' organisations in 65+ countries opposing plantations, logging concessions and forest-offset schemes that displace forest communities. USE IT where a project is marketed as restoration or carbon offsetting but takes community land.
